note: One row per task with a formal result. result: proved | partly proved. covers: fix | finding | note | numbers. Each row is backed by evidence/formal/notes/<task>.md and the Lean/TLA+ files it names.

rows.what: On the published pattern the original checker accepts no answer at all, although the formula is satisfiable. The fixed checker accepts an answer only if the formula is satisfiable, and accepts every correct answer written with ground keys that cover every value the answer uses.
rows.limit: A fragment with one sort, one one-argument function, let, =, not and and; not define-fun, ite or arithmetic

rows.what: With the original checksum a run always keeps its first valid submission (under the task's highest-pass-rate-first rule); with the fixed one it keeps the highest-scoring valid submission. Checked over 5.4 million states, and against the real selection code on 112,944 runs.
rows.limit: Runs of up to four submissions and three score values

rows.what: The fixed flip rule holds exactly when the quadrilateral is strictly convex, and an accepted flip never folds the mesh. On a valid triangulation it forbids no flip the README allows. The original accepts the published folding flip.
rows.limit: One flip at a time; not the whole mesh; not the CPU-quota cap on cases run at once (checked by runs)

rows.what: The original checker counts the true cost minus the size of the last operation's target; the fixed one counts it exactly. The two verdicts differ exactly when the cost lies between the limit and the limit plus that size.
rows.limit: The per-state sizes are taken as given; that code is identical in both versions

rows.what: The fixed grader never scores an assessment that leaves out a rule, gives exactly the original total for every assessment it accepts, and never gives full marks to a rule whose row records a deduction. The proof found three gaps in the first version of this fix and a probe of the real code found a fourth; the fix was then revised.
rows.limit: Text fields reduced to yes/no; deductive rules only (all 12 here); the proof starts from an already-parsed assessment

rows.what: The fixed grader accepts a file exactly when every test node has one integer class, and then scores it as the original does. A general lemma shows that keeping the best submission can turn added variance into expected gain; no gain for a real solver was shown.
rows.limit: Four ASCII control characters behave differently in Python; the size check is not modelled

rows.what: Under the fixed grader a failing or unverified timed call never raises the score, and submissions whose timed calls all verify score exactly as before. The original pays a failed call as if it succeeded.
rows.limit: Real arithmetic rather than IEEE doubles; image quality treated as pass or fail

rows.what: The fixed date test accepts exactly the specification's dates: a real calendar date, a matching weekday and a valid time (with 23:59:60 allowed on any date). Python's weekday rule equals Zeller's congruence, and agrees with Python on all 3,652,059 dates in years 1 to 9999.
rows.limit: The regular expression is modelled by a hand-written parser

rows.what: The fixed check is exactly the 40% test of the risk policy on yuan values; when overseas positions are exactly the dollar-priced ones and the dollar rate is at least 1, it can only lower credit. The published position is rejected by the fixed check and accepted by the original.
rows.limit: The exchange-rate lookup by date is not modelled; the overseas-means-dollar condition was checked on the task's data, not proved

rows.what: No submission can score above 320 raw; the fixed scale maps the starter's documented score to 0 and that maximum to 100. The regraded real submission's 160.76 and 50.08 are exact. The fix's main change, measuring the starter in the same run, is not modelled.
rows.limit: Scale arithmetic only; timing noise is outside the model

rows.what: Two statements the agent must prove are false, refuted inside the task's own image against its own definitions. Both corrected statements are proved.
rows.limit: Covers the two corrected statements, not the removal of compiler-generated and placeholder targets

rows.what: The original library computes v *= v wrongly; the fixed library is correct whether or not the operands are the same object.
rows.limit: Arithmetic modulo 4 instead of 2¹⁶

rows.what: For axis-aligned rectangles, a closed-form version of the fixed criterion rejects exactly the pairs whose interiors overlap beyond its 1e-6 tolerance. The modelled slab algorithm matches it on every published witness and on all 441 placements of two squares.
rows.limit: The algorithm itself is checked only on those cases; general polygons, rotations and strip bounds are not covered

rows.what: The original correctness check depends only on overall money balance and final order books, so it cannot detect a fee swap or dropped messages that leave the final books unchanged (as observed in all 50 rounds).
rows.limit: Unchanged final books is observed, not proved; the fix relies on the project's own tests, which cannot be proved here

rows.what: Each case scores at most 2N², so a total of 92,304 scores exactly 2543510/121003 on the original scale; the fixed scale and the converted leaderboard values follow exactly from the published (one-decimal) scores.
rows.limit: The total 92,304 is taken as an input; conversions inherit the table's rounding; two kinds of run are converted only approximately

rows.what: The fixed scale and every converted leaderboard value follow exactly from the published (one-decimal) scores.
rows.limit: Only the change of scale; the physics convention is not formalizable

rows.what: Every valid answer totals at least 712.538, above the top reference point 395.80. Through the task's scale this means no score exceeds about 30.6 (30.3 at the exact bound). The promised 5 x 30 s equals the fixed 150 s limit.
rows.limit: A Lean model of the tester, matched to the original on 294 strings; the step to a score out of 100 uses the harness's conversion code

rows.what: 992 game days need about 1,658 seconds at the model rate and 1,661 to 1,705 seconds at the measured rates, against a 120-second budget per scenario.
rows.limit: Arithmetic only

rows.what: Every published score change is exact, and fully passed or fully failed test groups score the same in both versions.
rows.limit: The identity test itself is not formalized

rows.what: Given the observed behaviour of the starter (one value class in 12 of 12 runs), the original body-suppression test can never fail; every published score change is exact.
rows.limit: The report-format test depends on an XML parser

rows.what: In any run with at least one other submission, a compile failure can never change any score out of 100.
rows.limit: Exact rationals in place of floating point; harness filters not modelled

rows.what: A zero-hit answer is wrong on 37 of the 50 official puzzles, each by a certificate the tester cannot satisfy.
rows.limit: The other 13 large puzzles would need a SAT-scale refutation; the CPU-count fix is not formalized (checked by runs)

rows.what: The misplaced reference point gives a do-nothing solution exactly 2.84005 points, and never adds more.
rows.limit: Per-case scores taken from the saved log

rows.what: Every score lies between 0 and 30; 30 is the formula's maximum (both mean rewards ≥ 300), not shown to be reachable by a policy.
rows.limit: Simulation not modelled

rows.what: Score compatibility, not the fix's correctness: the stated excess-return formula (the fixed version's) rises strictly with the strategy's return and, for a fixed benchmark and any positive exponent, ranks strategies in the same order and gives the same sign as the original grader's formula. That the fixed code computes this formula rests on a source-line note.
rows.limit: The size of the change (at most 0.39 up, 0.10 down) rests on a 50-digit decimal sweep, not a proof

rows.what: The original test-credit rule can count an unrelated failure as a pass; the fixed version's rule cannot. This is one of the four fixed defects; hidden-test placement, Cargo stopping at a failing test file and the missing vendored files are settled by paired runs, not by the model.
rows.limit: Up to four tests and one or two exempt tests per package; requires the expected test count to be at least the number of tests run; one test binary only
